narrative: The model estimated a 17.0% probability that you will fail your final year. In practical terms, that is a risk flag rather than a certainty: most students with a similar profile would pass, but the school treats this level of risk as sufficient to require remedial courses. The strongest influences on the estimate were your past record of no class failures, your intention to pursue higher education, and your mother's education. Importantly, all three pushed the prediction toward passing, not failing. Your zero past failures was the most influential factor and reduced your estimated failure risk most strongly. Your clear intention to continue to higher education was the second strongest factor and also worked in your favour; every passing student in the comparison group shared that goal. Your mother's secondary education was the third strongest factor and slightly reduced the risk, although higher maternal education is more common among students who pass. Because these leading factors are protective, the remaining 17% risk reflects the overall mix of your circumstances rather than those top items. To improve your position, keep your coursework stable, protect your record of no failures, maintain your higher-education goal, and address your 14 absences, which is well above the typical 3.78, so you can reduce the risk that triggered remedial support.
